svg.text: The largest of the last W — stack and heap at every step
9 ticks, W = 3 · scan 21 reads vs 16 steps · 2 of 7 windows span more than 6
2 // primitive: TICKS — the values, in the order they arrive. Written index:value.
4 // primitive: W = 3 — how many of the most recent to consider.
5 // primitive: L = 6 — the spread the second half must warn about.
6 // primitive: dq — a list of INDEXES, open at both ends. Indexes, not values, because
7 // only an index says whether an entry has left the window yet.
9 // primitive: back(dq) / front(dq) — the newest and oldest index held.
11 // primitive: dropBack(dq) / dropFront(dq) — remove from either end, in one step.
13 // primitive: dq.pushBack(i) — append one index to the newest end.
15 // primitive: evictLarger(dq, xs, i) — the mirror of evictSmaller, for the MINIMUM: drop
16 // anything at the back that is no SMALLER than the arriving value.
18 // primitive: allWindows(f) — run f over every window in turn, for comparison.
20 // primitive: NONE — no answer yet, because fewer than W ticks have arrived.
23 // "A risk screen shows the HIGHEST value among the last W ticks, updated on every
24 // tick. Millions of ticks; W up to 10^5. Update it without re-reading the window.
25 // Then: also warn when the last W ticks span more than L, highest minus lowest."
27 // function: bruteMax(xs, i) — the answer everyone gives first: read the window.
29 // 7 windows x 3 reads = 21 reads in all
34 if (xs[i + k] > best) { best = xs[i + k] }
40 // function: evictSmaller(dq, xs, i) — anything at the back that is no larger than the
41 // arriving value can never be the maximum again, because the newcomer is both BIGGER
42 // and NEWER, so it outlives them. Drop them.
52 // function: expire(dq, i) — the front has left the window if its index is more than W
53 // behind. At most ONE can expire per tick, because the window moves by one.
60 // function: slideMax(xs) — one pass. Every index is pushed once and dropped once, so
61 // the total work is 16 steps for 9 ticks, not 21.
77 // function: slideSpread(xs) — the same thing twice: one list kept DECREASING for the
78 // maximum, one kept INCREASING for the minimum, advanced together.
99 // function: main() — the scan, the one list, then the two.
102 val fast = slideMax(TICKS) // 16 steps, same answer
103 val spread = slideSpread(TICKS) // 2 of 7 windows over 6
Spreads [4, 5, 5, 5, 8, 8, 5]: 2 over 6 and 5 under, so the test discriminates rather than firing always or never. Both minima are asserted against the
brute-force scan too — a second deque with one comparison left un-reversed is the easiest possible bug and it produces plausible numbers.
